extracted.intended_audience: persons interested in filing international PCT patent applications (prospective applicants, patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing, filing and processing an international (PCT) patent application during the international phase, including forms/boxes, search/examination procedures, publication, time limits, and related procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of Invention (Box No. I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title of the invention as entered in Box No. I of the Request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prescribed form includes Box No. I for the title; the Request form is prescribed and must be accepted by designated Offices. See notes to the Request Form (paragraphs 5.020–5.039).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants and Inventors (Boxes Nos. II and III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of applicant(s) and inventor(s) as required in Boxes II and III of the Request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate naming and identification are required; changes concerning applicant or inventor are addressed in Chapter 11 (paragraphs 11.018–11.022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent or Common Representative (Box No. IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of the agent or common representative in Box No. IV of the Request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation rules and requirements for agents/common representatives are set out in Chapter 11 (paragraphs 11.001–11.014) and Receiving Office Guidelines; appointment may be required in some national phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of States (Box No. V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of Contracting States (and regional designations) in Box No. V of the Request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations determine where the international application will have effect; regional patent routes (ARIPO, Eurasian, Euro, OAPI) are available via PCT (paragraphs 4.022–4.026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Claim and Restoration of the Right of Priority (Box No. VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming priority from an earlier application and procedures for restoration of priority as entered in Box No. VI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claim must satisfy time limits and documentary requirements; restoration conditions and notes in paragraphs 5.057–5.071.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Searching Authority (Box No. VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection/identification of the International Searching Authority (ISA) in Box No. VII of the Request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may indicate preferred ISA; ISAs are listed in Annex D and their languages/requirements must be respected (paragraphs 5.072–5.073D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations (Box No. VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations required from the applicant (e.g., about entitlement, agent, priority) to be made in Box No. VIII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes to declarations in paragraphs 5.074–5.083A explain content and legal effects; certain declarations may be required by designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check List (Box No. IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of the check list in Box No. IX confirming enclosures and compliance with formalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the check list to ensure required parts (description, claims, drawings, abstract, sequence listings if any) are present; see paragraphs 5.088–5.091.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature of Applicant or Agent (Box No. X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signature required on the Request form (Box No. X) by applicant, agent or representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature requirements and consequences of missing signature are discussed (paragraph 5.092); applicant unavailability or unwillingness to sign addressed in paragraph 11.027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes to the Request Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretative notes and guidance accompanying the Request form explaining how to complete each box and the legal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes clarify formal requirements, entitlement, and interplay with PCT Articles/Rules; see paragraphs 5.093 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Calculation Sheet and Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of fee calculation sheet and payment of international filing and other PCT fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International fees may be paid once, at one Office and in one currency; fee calculation and applicable fees are explained (paragraphs 5.093, 5.101, 5.184 and Schedule of Fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Description (specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and formal requirements of the description part of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must meet PCT formalities and national law considerations; further guidance in paragraphs 5.112–5.127 on adequate disclosure and incorporation by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and substantive requirements for the claims included in the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be clear and supported by the description; see paragraphs 5.128–5.163 for number/format/definiteness and for amendments under Article 19 and Chapter II.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements for drawings submitted with the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings must comply with prescribed standards (size, symbols, clarity); originals/copies requirements and exceptions are in paragraphs 5.164–5.174.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to include an abstract and its proper form/content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should concisely indicate the technical disclosure; rules and purpose described in paragraphs 5.175–5.183 and affect publication and search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Formal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional formal requirements for international applications (formatting, paper size, language, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prescribed form is used to harmonize formalities between Offices; see paragraphs 5.184–5.199 for miscellaneous formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office Processing (including International Filing Date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and checks performed by the receiving Office, and conditions for establishing the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office carries out formalities check and establishes filing date according to PCT rules; see Chapter 6 (paragraphs 6.001–6.060) for processing, record and search copy handling and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of International Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When and into which languages translations must be provided during international processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in a language not acceptable to the ISA or for publication, a translation may be required shortly after filing; details in paragraphs 6.005–6.012 and 4.014.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Defects and Incorporation by Reference of Missing Elements or Parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for correcting defects in the international application and for incorporation by reference of missing parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office may allow correction or incorporation of missing elements; paragraphs 6.013–6.023 explain mechanisms and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Copy and Search Copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations regarding submission and handling of the record copy and search copy of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and search copies are used for international processing and search; the Guide explains who files what copies and when (paragraphs 6.024–6.056).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and/or Amino Acid Sequence Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Special requirements for sequence listings when the invention involves nucleotide/amino acid sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings must follow prescribed formats; see paragraphs in Chapter 7 and specific instructions (7.005–7.012) and Annexes for sequence listing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on International Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope and limits of the international search that an ISA will carry out on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISAs apply internationally regulated standards and may limit search scope (e.g., excluded subject-matter, lack of unity); limitations discussed in Chapter 7 (7.001–7.032).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the application relate to one invention or a group of inventions linked so as to form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of unity can lead to partial searches and additional search fees/partial reports; Unity is a ground for search limitations and is explained in Chapter 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and Abstract (as search/publication inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: How title and abstract affect search and publication (accuracy and suitability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title/abstract must accurately reflect disclosure for publication and to assist searching authorities; see Chapter 7 topics on Title and Abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Search Report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA's report identifying prior art found and classifying citations relevant to novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISR provides a basis for applicant decision-making and national phase prosecution; established according to high international standards (paragraphs 4.004, Chapter 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Opinion of the International Searching Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary, non-binding written opinion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability accompanying the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written opinion helps applicants assess patentability early and may be basis for amendments or demand for Chapter II examination (paragraph 4.004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary International Search (SISA) — Request and Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional request by applicant for supplementary searches by other ISAs and the grounds on which such searches can be based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may file Form PCT/IB/375; SISA provides broader prior-art coverage and is explained in Chapter 8 (including boxes, fees and processing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the Claims Under Article 19
rubrics_metrics.description: The possibility and procedure for amending the claims after receipt of the ISR under Article 19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 amendments affect the published claims and may influence national phase examination; details in Chapter 8 and relevant paragraphs (8.013–8.017).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Publication and Communication to Designated/Elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of the international application by the International Bureau and communication of copies and reports to designated/elected Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau publishes the application and communicates ISR, SISAs and PCT reports to Offices upon request; see Chapter 8 and publication sections for timelines and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a Demand for International Preliminary Examination (Chapter II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements, timing and formality of filing a demand for international preliminary examination under Chapter II of the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand must be filed within prescribed time limits and include required boxes (identity, election, amendments); see Chapter 10 (paragraphs 10.004–10.043) and Notes to the Demand Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Demand — Boxes, Elections and Signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of the Demand form (Boxes I–VII) including identification of application, applicants, agent, basis for examination, election of States and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Box has specific informational/legal effects; notes and processing instructions are given (paragraphs 10.012–10.034). Fees for demand are set out in paragraphs 10.035–10.043.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for Chapter II (demand and examination fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees payable in connection with making a demand for international preliminary examination and for the examination itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees and fee calculation sheets for demands are provided; timing and payment methods explained (paragraphs 10.035–10.043).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of the Demand and International Preliminary Examination Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: How the International Preliminary Examining Authority processes the demand and conducts the international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination is based on ISR and written opinion; applicant may amend and engage in dialogue with the examiner; see Chapter 10 (10.044–10.073) for procedure and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Report on Patentability (Chapter II IPER)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report issued at the conclusion of international preliminary examination analyzing patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPER is a substantive document communicated to national/regional Offices and is influential in national phase prosecution (paragraphs 10.074–10.083).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by Agents and Common Representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and requirements governing representation of applicants by agents or common representatives before receiving and other Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities for representation, powers, and changes are in Chapter 11 (paragraphs 11.001–11.014); appointment of local agents may be required in national phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: How Offices and the International Bureau communicate with the applicant and address for correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct contact details are essential; procedures for correspondence and consequences of misaddressing are in paragraphs 11.015–11.017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes Concerning Applicant, Inventor, Agent or Common Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements for notifying and effecting changes in applicant, inventor, agent or representative details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notification and supporting evidence may be needed; see paragraphs 11.018–11.022 and Section references in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of Applicant or Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to follow where the applicant or inventor dies during international procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procedures for who may act, deadlines and documentation are provided (paragraphs 11.023–11.026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Unavailable or Unwilling to Sign Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to follow if applicant is unavailable or refuses to sign the international application or other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office and IB remedies and alternative measures are set out (paragraph 11.027), including use of agents in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of Obvious Mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for correction/rectification of obvious mistakes in the international application or subsequent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectification is possible under specified conditions; see paragraphs 11.033–11.044 for scope and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments of the Claims, Description and Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed amendments during the international phase (under Article 19, Article 34, Chapter II, etc.) to claims, description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing, form and effect of amendments (including text to be published) are specified in paragraphs 11.045–11.047A and relevant chapters on Article 19/34 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawals
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and effects of withdrawing the international application or parts thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal rules, potential restoration and effects on national phase are explained in paragraphs 11.048–11.061.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: How PCT time limits are computed (calendar rules, priority dates, exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limit computation rules and relevant examples are in Chapter 11 (paragraph 11.062) and the Administrative Instructions; a 30‑month national phase limit is generally applicable (paragraph 4.016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in the Mail Service
rubrics_metrics.description: How delays or irregularities in postal/mailing services affect PCT deadlines and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for when postage delays may be excused and remedies are in paragraphs 11.063–11.064.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse of Delay in Meeting Time Limits and Extension of Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which delay in meeting PCT time limits may be excused and when extensions are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific provisions (including Rules/Sections and paragraph references 11.065–11.065C and 11.065D) describe grounds and procedures for excuse or extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of Letters and Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and formal requirements for filing letters and supporting documents during the international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses, form, translation and timeliness requirements for filing are covered in paragraphs 11.066–11.071.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of International Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on confidentiality of international applications prior to publication and limits on disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications remain confidential until international publication; exceptions and confidentiality protections are set out in paragraphs 11.072–11.074.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to Deposited Biological Material
rubrics_metrics.description: How to reference deposited biological material in the international application and related requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where biological material is necessary for disclosure, references and deposit details must meet prescribed requirements (paragraphs 11.075–11.087 and Annexes on deposits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Sequence Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed format and content requirements for nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings submitted with the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings must follow specific form and computer-readable formats; see paragraph 11.088 and Annexes for technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of International Applications to Successor States
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to extend effects of international applications to successor States of former Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules for successor states are in paragraphs 11.089–11.093; applicants must follow procedural steps and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing Indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional indication of licensing information (e.g., licensees) in the international application or during processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where provided, licensing indications are handled under rules explained in paragraphs 11.102–11.108.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Party Observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and criteria for third parties to submit observations on patentability of published international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party observations can be filed in prescribed timeframes and may influence examination; see paragraphs 11.109–11.117 for filing, admissibility and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limit to Enter the National Phase (30‑month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: General time limit for entering the national phase: 30 months from the priority date unless special conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 1 April 2002 the default time limit is 30 months from priority date (earlier 20‑month limit in some cases unless a demand is filed before 19 months); national Chapters and Official Notices may have updates (paragraph 4.016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and Place of Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Languages accepted by receiving Offices and where an international application may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are filed in a language accepted by the receiving Office; filing generally at national/regional Office or directly with IB where permitted (paragraphs 4.009–4.010).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed Form for the International Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the prescribed PCT Request form and its acceptance by all designated Offices to avoid divergent formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prescribed form harmonizes formalities across Offices; applicants must use it and follow the notes to the form (paragraph 4.011 and section 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralised Payment of International Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibility to pay international fees once at one Office and in one currency when filing the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralised fee payment avoids needing to pay multiple national fees at filing; national/regional fees become due later if applicant enters national phase (paragraphs 4.012, 4.015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of ISR/Written Opinion/IPER for National Phase Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: How the international search report, written opinion and international preliminary report assist applicant decision-making and national prosecution strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favorable reports strengthen position in national/regional Offices; partly unfavorable reports allow claim modification or abandoning further national filings, saving costs (paragraphs 4.004–4.021).
